title: Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rav Yehudah’s student, citing Chullin 48b: Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak wished to go to Bei Chozai; he came before Rav Yehudah and said, “Let the Master show me where the branches [of the spinal cord] divide” — he said to him, “Come, I will teach you.” He is also mentioned in Megillah 10b: Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak opened this section with an introduction from here: “For we are slaves.”

notes.text: The supplied Chullin 48b locator remains in the translation. Named Davidson Chullin 45b instead contains Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak’s Bei Chozai journey and request to locate the spinal-cord branches. It writes Rabbi Yehudah where Hyman writes Rav Yehudah, and replies “bring me a kid”; those witness differences remain distinct from Hyman’s “come, I will teach you.” This resolves the reviewer’s nonlocation without erasing the old locator.
